    // The summed length of every welded strut of the lattice.
    TotalStrutLength(self: StrutLattice3D): Number
        => TotalLength(self.Struts);

    // The volume of an axis-aligned box; the denominator of relative density.
    // Zero or negative for an empty (inverted) box.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Bounds.
    EnvelopeVolume(b: Bounds3D): Number
        => (b.Max.X - b.Min.X) * (b.Max.Y - b.Min.Y) * (b.Max.Z - b.Min.Z);

    // The fraction of the envelope the struts fill, treating each strut as a
    // cylinder of the given radius: sum of pi * r^2 * length over the envelope
    // volume (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relative_density).
    //
    // This is the FIRST-ORDER estimate and an OVERESTIMATE: material where
    // struts meet at a node is counted once per strut, and the spherical joints
    // that close those meetings are not counted at all. It converges on the true
    // fraction as radius over strut length goes to zero, which is the slender
    // regime lattices are used in; at radii approaching a third of the strut
    // length it is no longer usable.
    RelativeDensity(struts: Array<Line3D>, radius: Number, envelope: Bounds3D): Number
        => Number.Pi * radius.Square * TotalLength(struts) / EnvelopeVolume(envelope);

    // The same first-order estimate for a graded lattice, with one radius per
    // strut. Radii is parallel to struts.
    RelativeDensity(struts: Array<Line3D>, radii: Array<Number>, envelope: Bounds3D): Number
    {
        var solid = struts.Count.MapRange(i => radii[i].Square * struts[i].Length)
            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, v) => acc + v);
        return Number.Pi * solid / EnvelopeVolume(envelope);
    }

    // The lattice's relative density at its own uniform strut radius.
    RelativeDensity(self: StrutLattice3D): Number
        => RelativeDensity(self.Struts, self.Radius, self.Bounds);

    //==
    // # Operators over a strut list
    //
    // Grading, trimming and warping all consume the welded strut list rather
    // than re-tiling, so they compose in any order and none of them is a second
    // tiling path. Read left to right: `lattice.Struts.Trimmed(solid)` is the
    // trimmed lattice, and `.StrutRadii(field)` grades whatever it is handed.

    // One radius per strut, all the same. The uniform case in the shape the
    // graded operators produce, so the two feed the same consumers.
    StrutRadii(struts: Array<Line3D>, radius: Number): Array<Number>
        => struts.Map(s => radius);

    // One radius per strut, read from a scalar field at the strut's midpoint.
    // The field's value IS the radius, in world units; nothing rescales it.
    StrutRadii(struts: Array<Line3D>, radius: IScalarField3D): Array<Number>
        => struts.Map(s => radius.Eval(s.Centroid));

    // One radius per strut, from a grading field whose value is a fraction: the
    // field is sampled at the strut midpoint, clamped to [0, 1], and used to
    // interpolate between the ends of `range`. The usual spelling for "thicker
    // where this field is high".
    StrutRadii(struts: Array<Line3D>, grading: IScalarField3D, range: NumberInterval): Array<Number>
        => struts.Map(s =>
            range.Start.Lerp(range.End, grading.Eval(s.Centroid).Max(0.0).Min(1.0)));

    // The struts whose midpoint lies inside a box. Whole struts are kept or
    // dropped — nothing is clipped, so the trimmed lattice keeps its welding and
    // a strut straddling the boundary survives or vanishes entire.
    Trimmed(struts: Array<Line3D>, region: Bounds3D): Array<Line3D>
        => struts.FlatMap(s => KeepSegment(region.Contains(s.Centroid), s));

    // The struts whose midpoint lies inside a solid described by a signed
    // distance field (distance <= 0, as Contains). Whole struts, as above.
    // Written through the interface member Eval, not Contains: the C# backend
    // emits Contains only for concrete implementers, so a call on this
    // interface-typed parameter would not compile (stdlib-460).
    Trimmed(struts: Array<Line3D>, solid: ISignedDistanceField3D): Array<Line3D>
        => struts.FlatMap(s => KeepSegment(solid.Eval(s.Centroid) <= 0.0, s));

    // The struts whose midpoint lies inside a solid described by a membership
    // predicate. Whole struts, as above; through Eval for the same reason.
    Trimmed(struts: Array<Line3D>, volume: IImplicitVolume3D): Array<Line3D>
        => struts.FlatMap(s => KeepSegment(volume.Eval(s.Centroid), s));

    // The struts with both endpoints carried through a point map. This is how a
    // lattice is conformed to something other than its box, and how a graded
    // CELL SIZE is expressed: warp the tiled struts rather than tile unevenly.
    // A map that is not injective folds the lattice onto itself.
    Deformed(struts: Array<Line3D>, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): Array<Line3D>
        => struts.Map(s => s.Deform(mapping));

    // The lattice conformed to a different box: the same cell and counts, filling
    // the new bounds. Cell size follows the new extent, so this stretches rather
    // than re-tiles.
    ConformedTo(self: StrutLattice3D, bounds: Bounds3D): StrutLattice3D
        => StrutLattice3D(self.Cell, bounds, self.Counts, self.Radius);

    // The lattice at a different uniform strut radius.
    WithRadius(self: StrutLattice3D, radius: Number): StrutLattice3D
        => StrutLattice3D(self.Cell, self.Bounds, self.Counts, radius);

    // The lattice at a different repetition count.
    WithCounts(self: StrutLattice3D, counts: IntegerVector3): StrutLattice3D
        => StrutLattice3D(self.Cell, self.Bounds, counts, self.Radius);

    // The lattice built from a different unit cell, keeping its placement.
    WithCell(self: StrutLattice3D, cell: LatticeUnitCell): StrutLattice3D
        => StrutLattice3D(cell, self.Bounds, self.Counts, self.Radius);

    // How many cells of the given target size fit along an extent; at least one.
    CellDivisions(extent: Number, size: Number): Integer
        => (extent / size).ToInteger.Max(1);

    // A lattice whose cells are as near cubic as whole counts allow: the longest
    // axis of the bounds is divided `divisions` times and the other two follow
    // that cell size. The ergonomic way to place a cell in a box without working
    // out the counts by hand.
    UniformLattice(cell: LatticeUnitCell, bounds: Bounds3D, divisions: Integer, radius: Number): StrutLattice3D
    {
        var ex = bounds.Max.X - bounds.Min.X;
        var ey = bounds.Max.Y - bounds.Min.Y;
        var ez = bounds.Max.Z - bounds.Min.Z;
        var size = ex.Max(ey).Max(ez) / divisions.Max(1).ToNumber;
        return StrutLattice3D(cell, bounds,
            IntegerVector3(
                CellDivisions(ex, size), CellDivisions(ey, size), CellDivisions(ez, size)),
            radius);
    }

    // The struts as a solid: the union of capsules of one radius. Explicit
    // rather than implicit, because it settles the radius and discards the cell
    // and the counts (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Conversions).
    ToSdf(struts: Array<Line3D>, radius: Number): StrutSdf3D
        => StrutSdf3D(struts, radius);

    // The struts as a graded solid: the union of capsules, one radius per strut.
    ToSdf(struts: Array<Line3D>, radii: Array<Number>): GradedStrutSdf3D
        => GradedStrutSdf3D(struts, radii);

    // The whole lattice as a solid at its own uniform strut radius. Tiles once,
    // then evaluates against the resulting strut list.
    ToSdf(self: StrutLattice3D): StrutSdf3D
        => StrutSdf3D(self.Struts, self.Radius);

    // The distance to a lattice solid: the nearest capsule's distance. Exact —
    // a capsule distance is exact and the minimum of exact fields is the exact
    // distance to their union outside the solid.
    Eval(self: StrutSdf3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => self.Struts.Reduce(Number.MaxValue, (acc, s) =>
            acc.Min(DistanceToCapsule(point, s.A, s.B, self.Radius)));

    // The distance to a graded lattice solid: the nearest capsule's distance,
    // each strut taking its own radius. Exact, as above.
    Eval(self: GradedStrutSdf3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => self.Struts.Count.MapRange(i =>
                DistanceToCapsule(point, self.Struts[i].A, self.Struts[i].B, self.Radii[i]))
            .Reduce(Number.MaxValue, (acc, d) => acc.Min(d));
